chunks: From him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira who said:
I heard one of our companions mention that the minimum that suffices in the combat prayer, from the Takbir, is two Takbirs for each Salat, except for Maghrib, for it there are three.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of Takbirs required in the combat prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* specifies the minimum ritual validity (*ikhtisas*) for the combat prayer (*Salat al-Musafah*), establishing a baseline of two Takbirs for Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha, while uniquely requiring three for Maghrib. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle of easing religious obligations during times of military urgency (*darura*), allowing soldiers to maintain ritual purity even when time or safety is compromised. It highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh to adapt formal worship structures to the practical realities of battlefield conditions.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al-Mugheira who said,

‘I heard one of our companions mention that what would suffice during a time of the fencing, from the exclamations of the Takbīr, is two exclamations of Takbīrs for each Salāt, except for Al-Maghrib, for it there are three’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:

“I have heard from certain persons of our people saying that the minimum recitation when swords are at work is two Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) for every Salah (prayer) except that there are three Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) for al-Maghrib.”
